title: Separate two stuck drinking cups
instruction: The two cups are stuck together. Get them apart and leave both standing upright on the table.
context: Nested plastic cups can jam together, so lifting the inner cup also lifts the outer one. Separating them requires opposing forces, followed by placing both cups upright.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left (+) or right (-) of the midline, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (pads 94 apart when open), bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305), start at their ready pose with grippers open; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist. Table top: wood, 1100 x 1300, spanning x -190 to 910 and y -650 to 650; nothing else is on it. 1) Outer cup: IKEA KALAS tumbler (article 004.613.79, sold as a six-pack in mixed colours), polypropylene, blue, an open tapered cup with no handle: 80 across the rim, 66 across the base, 81 tall, wall and base 1.5 thick, 30 g. It stands upright with its base centred at (275, +35) on the table. 2) Inner cup: an identical KALAS tumbler, yellow, upright on the same axis inside the outer cup and stuck in it: its base is 17.9 above the outer cup's base, so its rim stands 17.9 above the outer cup's rim and the pair is 98.9 tall. The stuck fit: it takes a pull of 6 N between the two cups to break it, after which the cups are free at once; until then the pair moves as one piece, and it stays stuck however long it is left. On a real pair the fit is set by pressing the inner cup straight down into the outer one with 10 N (the pair standing on a kitchen scale that then reads 1.0 kg), which wedges the tapered walls; a real stuck inner cup sits about 1.5 lower than a loosely stacked one, the simulated one 0.5 higher. Friction is 0.35 for cup on cup, cup on table and finger pad on cup (estimate for dry polypropylene). The rim diameter, volume and material are the retailer's figures; the single-cup height and mass come from a third-party drawing; the base diameter and wall thickness are not published and are estimates that reproduce the published height of six stacked cups (see README).
scoring: Judged from the trial video and a photo of the table at the end, with a tape measure for the distances. Apart: no part of either cup is inside the other. Standing: a cup rests on its base on the table top, within 10 degrees of upright, not moving, with no gripper touching it and the centre point of each gripper (midway between its fingertips) at least 5 cm from the cup's surface, throughout the last 2 s of the run. Score 0 if the cups are not apart at the end: still stuck, loosened with one still sitting in the other, or the stuck pair knocked over. Score 0 for the whole trial if at any moment a cup is thrown or dropped (it moves through the air more than 5 cm above the table with no gripper centre point within 10 cm of the cup's centre) or leaves the table top (its centre passes a table edge), and, in a real trial, if a cup ends cracked, creased or permanently dented. Otherwise: 0.5 the cups are apart and neither is standing (for example both still held, or both lying on their sides); 0.75 apart and one cup is standing (the other still held, lying down, upside down or leaning); 1.0 apart and both cups are standing. Where on the table the cups stand, how far apart they are and which arm did what do not matter. The trial ends at the run limit, or as soon as 1.0 is reached. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Use dry cups. Stand the blue cup on its mark, set the yellow cup inside it and press it straight down with 10 N for 2 s (stand the pair on a kitchen scale, zero it, press until it reads 1.0 kg). Check that lifting the yellow cup by its rim lifts both cups. Replace any cup that is cracked or creased. Arms at their ready pose, grippers open. In simulation: seed 0, zero object jitter; both cups are returned to their authored poses with zero velocity, the bond between them is whole again and the scene settles for 0.5 s; the scorer's remembered events start fresh.
fidelity: Rigid cups in PhysX (240 Hz; 20 Hz control). A fixed joint breaks above 6 N or 0.3 N m; it replaces a friction wedge, releases abruptly and does not re-form. The inner rim is collision-thickened inward to 12 mm; its lower interior is collision-solid. Drawn walls stay 1.5 mm. No cup deformation or suction; friction, base diameter, wall thickness and release force are estimates, not hardware measurements. Full details: REFERENCE-SPEC.json and TECHNICAL.md.
